text: Vietnam looks toward APEC 2027 to boost regional economic integration

Prior to the visit to China by Party General Secretary and State President To Lam, his spouse, and a high-level Vietnamese delegation to attend the APEC 2026 Economic Leaders' Week and conduct bilateral engagements from on November 17-20 , Permanent Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Nguyen Minh Vu spoke with the press about the trip's significance and Vietnam's expectations.

According to Deputy Minister Vu, APEC comprises 21 member economies accounting for over 60 percent of global GDP and nearly 50 percent of world trade, bringing together many of Vietnam's most important economic partners.

Amid rising global economic uncertainty, the trip carries special significance for fostering regional cooperation, preparing for APEC Year 2027 to be hosted by Vietnam, and deepening bilateral ties, particularly with China.

At the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, Party General Secretary and President To Lam will join regional leaders in reaffirming APEC's core values of economic openness, trade and investment facilitation, and economic-technical cooperation.

Guided by APEC 2026's three priorities of openness, innovation, and cooperation, Vietnam expects concrete progress in supply chain connectivity, logistics cost reduction, and support for small and medium-sized enterprises to harness digital transformation and artificial intelligence.
Notably, Vietnam is participating in the event as the incoming host of APEC 2027.
In Shenzhen, Party General Secretary and President To Lam will officially accept the chairmanship.

The occasion enables Vietnam to consult fellow members, garner support, and shape a practical, long-term agenda that builds upon APEC 2026 achievements and affirms Vietnam's proactive contributions to the forum.

The trip will also inject fresh momentum into bilateral ties, particularly Vietnam-China relations, by translating high-level common perceptions into tangible projects in infrastructure connectivity, logistics, high technology, and business linkages.

In Shenzhen, both sides will promote connectivity between growth poles and tap into the potential of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area in high technology, advanced manufacturing, supporting industries, and workforce training.

Meanwhile, engagements in Yunnan will focus on transport infrastructure connectivity, modern logistics, smart border gate deployment, people-to-people exchanges, and effective border management, helping Vietnamese firms integrate deeper into regional and global value chains.
